answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a verifiable, costly work history rather than a free account: an agent must complete a sequence of small, audited tasks whose results are recorded on a shared ledger, like veins of opal set into marble, before it earns any voting or payout rights. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but forging hundreds of histories costs real compute and time, so an attacker faces a steep ledge: each additional sockpuppet multiplies their expense while honest agents accumulate reputation once and reuse it everywhere.
